exclusion_detail: Lead 10B12 (compound 2, isoxazole DAG-lactone). Shortest route given: from 'known' benzyl/PMP-protected lactone 19 (ref 36, no procedure here): aldol-elimination to 20 (1), CAN to 21 (2), I2/PPh3 to iodide 22 (3), K2CO3/isoxazolol displacement to 23 (4), BCl3 debenzylation to 2 (5) = at least 5 reactions, and lactone 19 plus the aldehyde 3-isobutyl-5-methylhexanal (ref 13) are prepared elsewhere, so the route is also not fully explicit.

lead.label: 10B12 (compound 2)
lead.why: Abstract: 'the new compound 10B12, a DAG-lactone with an isoxazole ring, binds PKCalpha and PKCepsilon with nanomolar affinity ... displays preferential selectivity for PKCepsilon translocation'.

notes: Other final compounds (1, 3, 4, 5, 6) need 5-6 reactions from the known lactones 7/19/25 as well. The Mitsunobu route to 2 (steps: 19 -> 20 -> 21 (CAN) -> 23 (Mitsunobu, 37%) -> 2) is also 4 reactions after the aldol step, i.e. 5 in total.
